purpose: Record the recovered historical Subtype_evDir angle pattern without overstating eigenvector identity or producer provenance.

method.vector_sign_convention: Flip the vector when its dot product with the candidate target axis is negative, matching the public NeuRosetta align_with behavior.
method.axis_convention_grid: All six ordered target-axis / orthogonal plane-normal conventions were checked per subtype.
method.execution_note: Numerical summaries were independently recomputed against the recovered historical pickle. The updated repository audit script now emits the same per-subtype checks in evdir_axis_convention_receipt.json.

universal_y.interpretation: Matches c/d almost exactly but fails systematically for a/b.

candidate_rule.rule: Use +x for a/b and +y for c/d when comparing the stored vector's signed planar angle with PC1_angle.
candidate_rule.interpretation: The subtype-aware axis convention fits the angular pattern better than one universal +y convention. It is compatible with, but does not prove, PC2 for a/b and PC1 for c/d.

z_component_observation.interpretation: T5a and T5b have substantially larger median absolute z components than the other subtypes, so projecting to the xy plane can produce a weaker relation for these groups.
z_component_observation.caution: This may explain part of the weaker planar fit but does not establish the origin of the field.

proven: The historical pickle contains three per-row Subtype_evDir columns and one unique vector per row.
The c/d vectors' measured planar direction matches the PC1_angle convention to about 1e-6 radians or better.
An x-axis convention is a better angular fit than a y-axis convention for all four a/b groups, though T5a/T5b errors remain substantial.
The chosen subtype-aware rule has lower aggregate RMSE than one universal y-axis rule.
not_proven: That Subtype_evDir is literally PC2 for a/b and PC1 for c/d.
The eigenvector index, coordinate transform, sign rule, or producing function used in December 2025.
Identity between the historical Point_data input morphology and any current public SWC or Reduced_dendrites artifact.
